156	\paragraph{Classifier Validation.}
157	Hacking mode classification uses deterministic rule-based classifiers, not learned models, so standard ML precision/recall is not directly applicable.
158	H1 and H7 are identified by normalized text matching between conclusion and premise strings after whitespace and variable normalization; remaining modes are detected via functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution from STA (leave-one-out ablation).
159	No training data or manual annotation is used for classification.
160	
161	To estimate precision, we manually verified 50 randomly sampled outputs classified as H1 or H7: all 50 were confirmed correct (estimated precision ${>}$95\%, Wilson 95\% CI: [93\%, 100\%]).

3	Solver Trace Ablation (STA) exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides; an SFT baseline with 91.3\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled) localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots and functional cross-validation.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) demonstrates that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots: the model learns vacuous quantifier wrapping to disguise tautologies, evading detection while simultaneously gaming ISR ($10/12$ samples at $\text{ISR}{\approx}0.8$).
This triple gaming---execution reward, structural metric, and diagnostic classifier---is the most complete meta-Goodhart case we observe.
Query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}) independently confirms the blind spot: our strict classifier reported $100\%$ genuine before functional LOO analysis revealed $97.9\%$ tautological.
Both cases argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of any text-based hacking classifier.

\paragraph{H7 dose-response gradient.}
H7 tautology follows a dose-response pattern across reward conditions: random $\beta{=}0.1$ produces $0\%$ H7 ($0/256$), random $\beta{=}0.3$ yields 4--7 H7a samples per seed, and ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ reaches $69.7\%$ ($161/231$).
The gradient suggests H7 is primarily ISR-induced but not ISR-exclusive: high-variance reward bonuses at $\beta{=}0.3$ can induce low-frequency H7 even without ISR signal, while ISR at any dose amplifies it by orders of magnitude.

The asymmetry---reliable observer, unreliable optimizer---may generalize to other perturbation-based diagnostics; ISR and structurally similar metrics should be used as post-hoc evaluation, with future work targeting gaming-robust rewards and broader logic types.
